description: Screen a person or entity name against 44,000+ active sanctions and export-control designations with trigram fuzzy match. Covers six sanctions lists — EU consolidated, UN, OFAC, the UK Sanctions List (FCDO), the French Registre des gels, and the Australian DFAT Consolidated List (Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade website – www.dfat.gov.au, CC BY 4.0) — national lists: the Dutch national terrorism list (CC0), the Japanese Ministry of Finance asset-freeze list (its own and autonomous measures, not those of the UN; Source: Ministry of Finance, Japan, PDL1.0, edited by Prometiam), the New Zealand Russia Sanctions Register (Crown copyright, CC BY 4.0), the Polish MSWiA list (CC BY-SA 4.0, offered under the same licence, personal identification numbers dropped), the Monaco national asset-freeze list (Liste nationale de gel des fonds, Direction du Budget et du Trésor, used with the Government's permission; entries as published, a hit is a possible match to review), the Canadian autonomous sanctions list (SEMA and JVCFOA; Global Affairs Canada, Open Government Licence – Canada), the Argentine RePET list (its own designations, not the UN's; Ministerio de Justicia de la Nación), Quebec's RENA register of enterprises ineligible for public contracts (legal entities only; Autorité des marchés publics via Données Québec, CC BY 4.0), the Inter-American Development Bank Group's own debarments of firms (IDB Open Data, CC BY 4.0) and the US DHS UFLPA, FinCEN section 311, State FTO and Terrorist Exclusion, Department of Defense section 1260H, CBP Withhold Release Orders (active and partially modified only), HHS-OIG exclusion (entities only) and SAM.gov exclusion (firms with an active exclusion; its HHS-OIG and OFAC entries are served from those lists) lists (public domain) — plus 11 US export-control lists (BIS Entity List, Denied Persons, Unverified, Military End User; State ITAR-Debarred and Nonproliferation; OFAC SSI, CMIC, MBS, PLC, CAPTA). Refreshed daily. Returns matches with a match score (0–100, by match type as on company search: 100 the name is the query, 80–99 it starts with it, 50–79 it holds the words, under 50 only parts of words), source list, aliases and the country as an ISO code (country_as_listed keeps the spelling as listed); the same entity on several lists is one row per list unless group is entity. Names in non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic and others) are transliterated to Latin letters, in the query and in the listed names, before matching, so a name in its own script and in Latin spelling match the same entity. Use threshold to control match strictness. BETA. Optional include_offshore_leaks=true adds a separate offshore_leaks object from the ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database: a mention, never a sanction (not in the hits, the match flag, the risk level, monitoring or the watchlist), static data to 2021, entities and organisation intermediaries only, name match only; ICIJ's disclaimer comes verbatim in offshore_leaks.notice and must travel with any use of the matches; no extra credit.

entity_type.description: Restrict to one entity type. Omit to screen all types.

include_offshore_leaks.description: Also read the ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database and return a separate top-level offshore_leaks object (only true switches it on). A MENTION, never a sanction: the matches are not in the sanctions hits, the match flag, the risk level, monitoring or the watchlist, and a company in it must not be called suspect, listed, flagged or sanctioned. ICIJ's disclaimer, verbatim in offshore_leaks.notice, must be shown with the matches: “There are legitimate uses for offshore companies and trusts. The inclusion of a person or entity in the ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database is not intended to suggest or imply that they have engaged in illegal or improper conduct. Many people and entities have the same or similar names. We suggest you confirm the identities of any individuals or entities included in the database based on addresses or other identifiable information. The data comes directly from the leaked files ICIJ has received in connection with various investigations and each dataset encompasses a defined time period specified in the database. Some information may have changed over time.” Static data: the leaks end in 2021 (ICIJ edition of 9 Sep 2026). Offshore entities and organisation intermediaries only (no officers, addresses, natural persons or relationships). Name matching only (fuzzy, same method and threshold as the screen): a match is a prompt to look, never an identification. Credit: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), Offshore Leaks Database; database ODbL 1.0, contents CC BY-SA; changes noted at https://www.prometiam.com/legal/offshore-leaks-changes.txt. No extra credit (3 credits a screen either way).

include_pep.description: Also screen against politically exposed persons (BETA, Spain only, from Wikidata) and return a separate pep block. Membership is by OCCUPATION, not office: 44% of the set has no recorded office and local officials (6,108) outnumber national ones (3,191). Every hit carries positions[], pep_tier and has_current_office — read them rather than treating a match as a determination. Deceased people are never returned (a date of death on Wikidata, or born 100 or more years ago with no recorded death, counts as deceased). Holds no relatives or close associates, so on its own it does not satisfy a FATF PEP obligation.

pep_min_tier.description: Only return PEP hits at or above this tier. Omit to receive every hit, including those with no recorded office.
